title: Cache, sample, speculate
brief: Size and build a KV cache, implement the decoding rules that turn logits into text, and prove speculative decoding's acceptance rule out in code.
hints: kv_cache_bytes is 2 * n_layer * n_kv * d_head * seq_len * bytes_per_elt. The 2 is for keys and values, not for anything else.
KVCache.append should just grow a per-layer list of arrays; KVCache.get should np.stack whatever has been appended so far for that layer, along a new leading axis of length T.
apply_temperature divides the logits by temperature, then applies a numerically stable softmax (subtract the max before exponentiating).

nucleus_filter needs the smallest prefix of the probabilities, sorted from largest to smallest, whose cumulative sum reaches p. numpy.argsort(-probs) gives that order; numpy.cumsum and numpy.searchsorted find the cutoff without a Python loop.

speculative_accept: draw one uniform random number from rng, compare it to min(1, p[draft_token] / q[draft_token]). On rejection, build the residual np.maximum(p - q, 0), normalise it, and use rng.choice to sample from it.
